reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement instrument rather than a method: the substitution ratio S, quantifying how much of an ExpeL-style experience bank's benefit survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is given exactly the same training episodes, paired with a frozen whole-bank-compiled instruction arm that tests whether per-instance retrieval buys anything at all, and a near-duplicate positive-control bank that is supposed to make a null interpretable.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two uncited works threaten this more than anything in the proposal's related-work section. (1) Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429) already runs an offline variant in which workflows induced from the whole training set are placed statically in the prompt with no per-instance retrieval, and reports it competitive with the online retrieval variant on web agents. That is arm C and prediction 3 already executed, in a different environment, and the proposal presents the compiled-static arm as its risky non-obvious claim while never citing it. (2) MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., arXiv 2406.11695) is the canonical study of instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations as two containers optimized against the same trainset, and reports that the demonstration slot often carries most of the gain; that is the prior for the substitution question, and it points the opposite way from prediction 1. Also, ExpeL itself ablates distilled insights against retrieved raw trajectories, which is most of prediction 7 already. MemDelta, the only collision the proposal engages with, is genuinely a different confound and is handled correctly; the danger is on the prompt-optimization side, which the check never searched.
reviews.strongest_objection: The matched-information constraint does not do the work claimed for it, because information is matched but optimization pressure is not. I1 is produced by 300 scored rollouts of hill-climbing with validation-guided candidate selection across 3 seeds; B is produced by a single non-iterated distillation pass over 500 episodes with no validation-guided curation, pruning, or best-of-N selection. So cell 6 minus cell 5 compares a searched artifact against an unsearched one, and the headline S >= 0.6 is fully explained by search beats no search, which says nothing about containers and which no memory-systems author would accept as a fair test of their system. The iso-cost curve does not repair this: growing the bank with more episodes at fixed distillation is not optimizing the bank. Second, and nearly as damaging, the precheck gate is a selection-on-noise device: a bank that fails is enriched until it clears +10 points on a 150-instance dev split, where the sampling SE of a paired gain is roughly 4 points, so the surviving bank is selected for upward noise; that inflates the denominator of S while the numerator is not similarly selected, biasing S toward 1 in exactly the direction predicted, with no stopping rule, no pre-registered enrichment budget, and no compute line for the enrichment loop. Third, the design cannot confirm its own prediction 3: the stated single-pair MDE is ~4 points and the proposal commits to reporting sub-MDE differences as inconclusive, yet prediction 3 asserts a difference under 2 points with no equivalence test specified. Under the proposal's own decision rule prediction 3 can be refuted but never confirmed, and TOST at plus-or-minus 2 points would need several times n=600.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Add a memory-side optimization arm so the comparison is symmetric: curate the bank against the same 150-instance dev split with a call budget matched to GEPA's 300 rollouts (validation-guided pruning, best-of-N banks, or ReasoningBank-style self-judged refinement), and report S against both the naive and the optimized bank. Replace enrich-until-pass with a pre-registered bank plus a pre-registered enrichment budget, compute the gate on a split disjoint from the one used for the S denominator, and report S for the pre-registered bank whether or not it clears 10 points. Titrate B-dup so its I0 gain lands near the same 10-point regime as the real bank, otherwise the positive control lives in an effect-size regime where no ceiling or headroom argument bites and it cannot license the null-is-a-finding claim at the effect size that matters. Add a headroom control (an instruction that matches I1's accuracy but is built from information other than the training episodes, for example GEPA on a disjoint task pool), since I3 controls verbosity only and diminishing returns at higher baseline accuracy is a complete alternative explanation for a high S. Restate prediction 3 as a formal equivalence test with its own power calculation, or as a one-sided bound. Finally, cite and ideally replicate Agent Workflow Memory's offline setting as the precedent for arm C, and reconcile the +10 gate with the track's own prior finding that this bank fixed zero items and broke six or seven.
reviews.missing_baseline: An optimized-memory arm: a bank curated or selected against the same dev split under a call budget matched to GEPA's rollouts, so that the study compares optimized instruction against optimized memory rather than optimized instruction against a one-pass distillation. Secondary and also absent: an accuracy-matched instruction control derived from information other than the training episodes, needed to separate substitution from ordinary diminishing returns at a higher baseline; I3 pads length but not accuracy.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually candid and partly credible: it names MemDelta as a partial collision on framing, correctly argues that MemDelta's confound is inside the retrieval pipeline rather than a rival container, and it retracts five citations from an earlier draft as unverifiable. But candor is not coverage, and the check is one-sided. Every search it reports is on the memory-audit side; it never searched the prompt-optimization side, which is where the real collision sits, and it therefore misses Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429), whose offline whole-corpus workflow induction with no per-instance retrieval is essentially arm C and largely anticipates prediction 3, and MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695), the standing prior on instruction-versus-demonstration substitutability. It also concedes it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 and cannot verify TERMS-Bench, which it itself identifies as the closest structural precedent for the central logical move of using a prompt optimizer as the control for a non-prompt intervention. A further problem for a reviewer: the entire related-work section rests on 2026 arXiv identifiers (2606.29914, 2601.22964, 2603.18272, 2605.21768, 2603.02473) that cannot be checked from the submission, and the admission that a previous draft cited five works that do not appear to exist lowers confidence in the remainder. The check is above average for this venue but it has not established novelty on the axis where novelty is actually at risk.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement paper that defines a substitution ratio S — the fraction of an ExpeL-style bank's paired memory gain that disappears once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is given exactly the same training episodes — and adds a frozen 'compile the whole bank into one static instruction and delete retrieval' arm (C/M2) plus a deliberately non-compilable near-duplicate bank (B-dup) so that a null on S is interpretable rather than a power failure.
reviews.closest_prior_work: ExpeL itself (2308.10144), which the proposal treats only as a target. ExpeL's pipeline already separates two containers — extracted insights, which are appended statically to the instruction, and retrieved successful trajectories used as demonstrations — and its own ablations report both contributing. Arm C ('a frontier model reads the entire bank offline and compiles it into one static instruction block, no retrieval at inference') is close to ExpeL-insights-only, and ExpeL's published ablation is direct evidence against Falsifiable Prediction 3. The Related Work section never mentions this ablation, which is the single most damaging omission in the novelty argument. Two further real precedents are unaddressed: (a) MIPROv2/DSPy already optimizes instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations as separable slots and reports instruction-only vs demo-only vs joint ablations — that is a published controlled comparison of exactly the two containers the proposal claims the field has never compared; (b) Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024) induces reusable workflows from training episodes in an offline setting and injects them as static prompt text, which is arm C for web agents. None of these individually make S novel, but together they mean the 'compile, don't retrieve' prediction is a re-test of existing ablations rather than a new hypothesis, and only the matched-information constraint and the ratio endpoint remain genuinely new.
reviews.strongest_objection: The design cannot confirm its own headline predictions, by the authors' own stated rules. Measurement gives a per-cell-pair MDE of ~4 points at n=600 and ~5.6 points for a change in the memory gain, and Limitation 6 commits to reporting sub-MDE differences as 'inconclusive in either direction.' But Prediction 3 — which the proposal itself calls 'the risky, non-obvious prediction' — asserts that I0xM2 comes 'within 2 points' of I0xM1; Prediction 7 asserts I0xM1 exceeds I0xM3 by '<3 points'; Prediction 2 asserts I3 recovers '<20% of I1's improvement' (about 1 point if I1-I0 is ~5). All three are equivalence claims strictly inside the MDE, and no equivalence procedure (TOST, a declared margin, a power calculation for equivalence) appears anywhere in Measurement and Noise Control — only NHST with McNemar and Holm. A non-significant I0xM2 vs I0xM1 difference will therefore be reported as 'compilation matches retrieval' when it is simply absence of evidence, and applying Limitation 6 honestly means Predictions 2, 3 and 7 can be refuted but never confirmed. Only Predictions 1, 4 and 6 are resolvable at this power. Compounding this, the primary endpoint's denominator is not measured but manufactured: the PRECHECK GATE says a bank that fails the 10-point dev gate 'is enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes.' That does two bad things. It selects the denominator on a 150-instance dev split for being large, so the test-split denominator regresses downward and the whole MDE argument ('the predicted drop of ≥6 points sits above the MDE') may not hold when S is actually computed; and adding training episodes to the bank breaks the equal-training-episode constraint that Experiments calls 'the fairness constraint that makes the study interpretable,' since GEPA is not re-run on the enriched split. A reviewer will also note the internal tension with the track's own starting position: at k=7 a full retrieved bank was measured to fix zero items and break six to seven, yet this plan fixes top-k=7 and requires a +10-point gain from it before any cell is run.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Pre-register the bank: freeze construction before any dev measurement, forbid the enrichment loop, and if the gate must exist, gate on a split disjoint from both optimization and test and report the shrinkage. Better, replace the gate with a rule that S is reported only when the test-split denominator's lower CI bound exceeds 8 points, and otherwise report the two paired differences separately instead of their ratio. 2) Re-specify Predictions 2, 3 and 7 as equivalence tests with a declared margin and a power calculation for that margin; at a 2-point margin on paired binary outcomes this likely needs n well above 600 or a matched-pairs design with more decoding seeds, and it is better to know that now than to publish a sub-MDE tie as a match. 3) Restore I2 and add a k sweep (see missing_baseline). 4) Add a no-episode instruction-rewrite control so the matched-information premise is actually tested. 5) Drop Prediction 5 or power it — a top-decile subgroup is n=60 against a ~4-point MDE, so 'the bottom 70% shows a residual gain whose CI covers zero' is guaranteed regardless of truth. 6) Verify every 2026 citation by hand and report which were confirmed, given the retraction of five in the previous draft. 7) Fix the incoherent 'token-matched per instance' spec for the static arm C: a frozen block cannot vary per instance without becoming a retrieval system, so state whether the match is on the mean and what is truncated.
reviews.missing_baseline: A no-episode instruction-rewrite control: an instruction produced by the same frontier model from the task description and the hand-written I0 alone, with zero access to any training episode, token-matched to I1. Without it, a high S is equally explained by 'a frontier model wrote a better scaffold for a 14B agent' as by the paper's thesis that instruction and memory are two containers for the same episode-derived information; I3 padded with 'task-generic boilerplate' controls length, not content provenance, so the causal claim about matched information is untested. Two further omissions a reviewer will demand: (a) a retrieval-budget arm (k=3 alongside k=7) — the track's own measured result is that injection volume, not memory content, was the causal lever, so fixing k=7 makes both the S denominator and the I0xM2-vs-I0xM1 verdict functions of an untuned hyperparameter, and a compiled-static win over k=7 that vanishes against k=3 refutes the practical recommendation; (b) I2, GEPA optimized with memory in context, which is cut as 'co-adaptation, not substitution' but is the only realistic deployment pairing — measuring memory's residual on top of an instruction that was optimized to work without memory biases the numerator of S downward and S upward, and it is question 4 of the track brief.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check has the right shape — it names a closest work, separates genus from claim, states residual risk, and openly retracts prior citations — and that self-correction is more than most submissions do. But it does not establish novelty. Every load-bearing 2026 reference (MemDelta 2606.29914, EvoClinician 2601.22964, 2603.02473, 2605.21768, 2603.18272) is unverifiable to me, and the check itself reports that the previous draft cited five papers (ActMem 2603.00026, MAS-PromptBench 2606.23664, TERMS-Bench 2605.13909, MemAPO 2603.21520, 2602.11243) that the current search could not return and that all reliance on them was removed. A search tool demonstrated within this same document to emit references that cannot be re-found cannot then be trusted to certify that the closest work is MemDelta; the correct remedy is per-citation manual verification with a stated confirmation status, which is absent. The check also concedes it never swept OpenReview 2026 — the single most likely home for a 'GEPA vs memory bank' ablation, given GEPA is itself an ICLR 2026 oral — and the flagged TERMS-Bench, described as a GEPA-based substitution test for a non-prompt intervention, would be a direct precedent for the logical move if it exists. Most importantly, the check searches only for collisions on framing and misses the collisions that actually bite, which are ablations inside the papers being targeted: ExpeL's insights-only versus retrieved-demonstrations ablation, MIPROv2's instruction-versus-demonstration ablations in DSPy, and offline workflow induction in Agent Workflow Memory. Net: a thin check on the axis that matters, and I treat the novelty claim as unestablished rather than merely unverified.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement study that asks how much of a procedural experience-memory bank's benchmark gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) has been given the same training episodes, operationalized as a substitution ratio S, plus the stronger engineering claim that the whole bank can be compiled once, offline, into a frozen instruction and per-instance retrieval deleted with no loss.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three lines threaten it, none of which the proposal cites. (a) ACE / Agentic Context Engineering (arXiv 2510.04618) treats an accumulating natural-language playbook as the container for training-episode experience and benchmarks it directly against GEPA on agent tasks, which contradicts the proposal's claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other'. (b) Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv 2504.07952) and Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429, offline variant) already build a single static distilled text artifact from past episodes and inject it with no per-instance retrieval, which is exactly arm C; AWM's offline-vs-online comparison is a weak-form version of prediction 3 and it already reports offline induction is competitive. (c) ExpeL itself (2308.10144) ablates its global insight list against its retrieved trajectory pool, so 'do the retrieved per-instance items add anything over the globally injected distillate?' is partly an existing ExpeL ablation. What survives as new is the specific accounting object (substitution ratio at matched training episodes and matched injected tokens) and the non-compilable positive control, which is a real but modest contribution.
reviews.strongest_objection: S is not diagnostic of the mechanism the paper names. On a bounded accuracy scale, any intervention that raises the no-memory baseline by a large amount will shrink a second intervention's marginal gain through simple saturation and sub-additivity in accuracy space, whether or not the two containers hold the same information. The design has no arm that separates 'I1 already contains memory's information' from 'memory's gain shrinks on top of any stronger baseline'. I3 controls prompt length, not baseline strength, and the primary endpoint is computed on the raw accuracy scale even though the CIs come from a logistic model, so an effect that is perfectly additive in logits will be reported as S near 0.5-0.7 and written up as substitution. Second, the design fails on its own arithmetic: with the stated SE of 2.0 points on the numerator and roughly 1.4-2.0 on a denominator gated at 10 points, the delta-method SE on S is about 0.2, so a 95 percent bootstrap CI has half-width near 0.4; prediction 1 requires a point estimate of 0.6 whose CI excludes 0.3, which is unattainable at n=600 with 3 optimizer seeds unless the true S is 0.75 or higher. The proposal's own 'cannot resolve S better than roughly plus/minus 0.2' is a one-SE number being read as a confidence interval.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an information-mismatched but strength-matched instruction arm: GEPA run on a disjoint task pool (or on the same episodes with a scrambled reward signal), padded to the same length and selected to deliver a comparable I1-vs-I0 gain. If memory's gain collapses on top of that instruction too, S measures saturation, not substitution; if it survives, the informational reading is earned. An accuracy-matched non-prompt strengthener (self-consistency, larger step budget) is an acceptable second form of the same control. (2) Demote S to a descriptive secondary and make the primary endpoint the memory-by-instruction interaction term on the logit scale from the mixed-effects model already specified, which is the quantity that is actually additive. (3) Fix the fairness constraint in the protocol, not just the prose: the bank uses 500 E1 episodes while GEPA gets 300 rollouts, and the precheck permits enriching the bank with more training episodes until it clears 10 points without re-running GEPA on the enlarged split. As written this both violates 'exactly the same training episodes' and tunes the denominator of S upward on a dev split, which biases S toward the hypothesis. Freeze the bank before any gate readout, or pre-register the enrichment rule, re-run the optimizer on the final split, and report S for every bank built. (4) Convert predictions 2, 3 and 7 to formal equivalence tests (TOST) with margins above the MDE; as stated, 'within 2 points' on a design with a 4-point MDE is confirmed by failure to reject, which is the exact trap the Measurement section elsewhere avoids. (5) Re-power the positive control: predicting that I0xM2dup loses to I0xM1dup by at least 5 points on an n=300 subset whose stated MDE is about 6 points means the load-bearing instrument can fail to fire for power reasons, which destroys the 'a null is a finding' argument. Either seed B-dup to produce a much larger effect and say so, or run it at full n. (6) Resolve TERMS-Bench and cite ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet and Agent Workflow Memory.
reviews.missing_baseline: An instruction arm that is optimized but informationally disjoint from the memory bank: GEPA run on a held-out or unrelated task pool, or on the same episodes with a shuffled/scrambled metric, length-matched to I1 and chosen to produce a similar I1-vs-I0 accuracy gain. Without it, cell 6 (I1xM1) cannot distinguish container substitution from diminishing returns, and every headline number is compatible with both. A secondary omission: no faithful ExpeL configuration is run. M1 is described as top-k=7 retrieval over distilled insights plus condensed trajectories, whereas ExpeL injects its insight list globally and retrieves only trajectories; that difference means arm C (compiled static) is being compared against a variant of ExpeL rather than ExpeL, and a reviewer will ask whether the compiled-vs-retrieved result is an artifact of how M1 was assembled.
reviews.preprint_collision: Diligent in form, unreliable in substance, and with a specific known miss. The check does the right structural thing by retracting five previously cited works (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, 2602.11243) that the current search could not return, but that retraction is itself the problem: it establishes that the search tooling produced fabricated or unstable hits in at least one direction, which means the surviving citations (MemDelta 2606.29914, EvoClinician 2601.22964, 2603.02473, 2605.21768, 2603.18272) carry no more warrant than the retracted ones. The single most threatening item is then left unresolved by a conditional ('if that work exists as described'), when TERMS-Bench is precisely the structural precedent for the paper's core logical move. The check also states that no OpenReview 2026 sweep was performed, and it misses three verifiable 2024-2025 preprints that bear directly on the risky prediction: ACE (2510.04618), which already runs a GEPA-vs-accumulated-context comparison and therefore falsifies the Related Work sentence that no one has used one as a control for the other; Dynamic Cheatsheet (2504.07952); and Agent Workflow Memory (2409.07429), whose offline variant is arm C under a different name. Given that these are exactly the neighborhood the check was supposed to sweep, I treat the novelty of the compiled-static instrument as unestablished rather than merely uncertain.
